header: THE BENGALI FRONT PAGE, HAND-CURATED. The Bengali tab is the one most of the plant's readers will stay on, so I do not make it a plain list of the newest headlines: I choose it like the front page of a newspaper, from SEVERAL Bengali dailies, with Anandabazar Patrika (the local paper, read section by section through Google News) at the top priority and the others mixed in with it: Anandabazar Patrika, Sangbad Pratidin, Bartaman, Ei Samay, Aajkaal, and BBC বাংলা. WHAT COMES FIRST, in each paper's own stories, by DESKS in an order of importance: TOP BAND (tier 1, chosen first) attack a militant attack war a war demise a death announced as one (প্রয়াত, প্রয়াণ) trending a story that THREE OR MORE papers carry CORE (tier 2, in turns) politics 4 sports 3 metro 2 business 2 FILL (tier 3, what is left) the paper's other state, national and world news, entertainment I use the desks only to CHOOSE the stories; the card names no desk (the reader sees a headline, the paper and the time). HOW THE PAGE IS MIXED. The page has eighteen places, SHARED among the papers by their priority (SHARE below): Anandabazar six, Sangbad Pratidin, Bartaman and Ei Samay three each, Aajkaal two, BBC বাংলা one. Each paper puts forward its own stories in the order of the desks (one of each desk in turn, so its places are not all politics); I fill the places paper by paper in rounds, Anandabazar first in every round; a place a paper cannot fill (it has too few stories) goes to the papers in priority order, so Anandabazar is the first to take it. A story that two papers carry is ONE card, shown as the higher-priority paper's (src/lib/live/rss.ts), so the same news never appears twice. The top band holds at most six stories in all. WHAT A DESK IS. A story's section in the paper (Anandabazar's West Bengal, Kolkata, India, World, Sports and Business sections are read as separate feeds, src/lib/live/news.ts) is its default desk. The top-band desks and politics cut across sections, so I find them by words of the headline, and a few rules keep those words honest: a film or a sports headline is never "war" or "attack" (the real data had a film scene and a sports match said to be wars), "Maoist" is not a word of attack (a drug campaign was called that), and "missile" alone is not a word of war (a missile-building programme). For the papers read as a whole (no sections) I tell sports and business stories by plain words (ক্রিকেট cricket, ফুটবল football, সেনসেক্স Sensex ...). The words are in ONE place below, and were tested against real headlines (fixtures/bn-headlines-2026-11-13.json and the papers' feeds). They are plain Bengali words whose meaning is known; this is a heuristic, not understanding. METRO. I read it both ways: the Kolkata city section, and any headline about the metro railway (মেট্রো). DEMISE. The words say a death was announced; they cannot tell a famous person from an ordinary one, so I let the reader's own sections come first. SHOWN ORDER. By TIME alone, the latest at the top, like every other tab: the desks and the papers' shares only decide WHICH stories are on the page, never where they stand.

symbols.sig: export function curate(stories: FeedItem[], limit = FRONT_PAGE): FeedItem[]
doc: The front page: `limit` stories, shown by time, the latest first (the band only decides which stories are chosen).

(1) THE TOP BAND I choose first, across all the papers: each of its desks gives its best story (the higher-priority paper's first, a death in the reader's own sections before a foreign one, then the newest), then a second, and so on up to the desk's quota, until the band holds TIER1_CAP. A paper holds at most half its share of places in the band (Anandabazar three, Sangbad Pratidin, Bartaman and Ei Samay two, the others one), so that the top of the page is a mix of papers; the rest of its band stories go down to the core and are shown among the others.

(2) THE REST is shared among the papers by SHARE, with the band stories counting HALF against the share of their paper (so a paper with several attacks to report still has places for its metro and business stories): one place of each paper in turn, Anandabazar first, each paper putting forward its own stories by desk; a place a short paper leaves goes to the papers in priority order.

behaviours: the desks are in the order of importance: the top band (attack, war, demise, trending), the core (politics, sports, metro, business), the fill
the quotas are politics 4, sports 3, metro 2, business 2, and the top band at most six in all, each of its desks that has a story given one place first
a desk has no name for the card: the cards carry no chip of what kind of news it is (the desks only choose and order the stories)
a militant attack in Kashmir on a CRPF camp is 'attack' (the word for militants, in the national section)
a terrorist attack in Kulgam that injured a man of Bishnupur is 'attack' too (from the West Bengal section)
a former minister's passing, announced with 'প্রয়াত', is 'demise'; so is the sudden death of a Russian ambassador (world)
a drug campaign 'in the manner of putting down Maoists' is NOT an attack ('Maoist' is no word of attack); a missile-building programme is NOT a war
a FILM scene 'on the battlefield' and a film's 'Sita's war' are NOT war: the entertainment section never is
the Iran war's effect on diesel (national section) is 'war'
a party and a chief minister's headline is 'politics' (in the West Bengal section, the Kolkata section and the national one)
a sports headline stays sports, even when it speaks of an election ('ক্রীড়াবিদদের নির্বাচনে লড়বেন'): the sports section is never read for politics
the Kolkata section is the metro desk, and a headline about the metro railway is metro whatever its section
business stays business; a plain crime story of the West Bengal section is 'state' (no rule catches it, so only its section is said)
a famous person's death in the sports or the film section is still 'demise' (the section does not hide it)

among deaths announced, the reader's own sections come first: with one place, a former state minister (West Bengal section) is chosen before a foreign ambassador (world), though the ambassador's is the newer; on a full page both are in the band, with the attacks and the war

in the top band the higher-priority paper has the first place and the larger share of a desk: with three places for attacks, an older Anandabazar attack is chosen before a newer Sangbad Pratidin one, Anandabazar gets two of the three and Sangbad Pratidin one
the places are SHARED by the papers' priority: six papers with plenty of stories give Anandabazar six, Sangbad Pratidin, Bartaman and Ei Samay three each, Aajkaal two, BBC বাংলা one
the shares add up to the front page, Anandabazar Patrika has the most and is first in the priority
a paper with too few stories leaves its places to the others in priority order, so Anandabazar takes them first (Bartaman and Aajkaal with none: Anandabazar gets 6 + 1, the rest by turns)
a mix of papers on the real data: Anandabazar's stories keep every top-band place they had, and no paper is left out of the page
one paper holds at most half its share in the top band: six attacks of one day give Anandabazar three places in the band (the rest go down to the core, still on the page)
the top of the page is a mix of papers: when several papers have news of a war or an attack, no paper holds more than half its share of the band
a story carried by three papers (the one shown and two others named) is 'trending'; by two it is not; a film story never is
the front page has eighteen distinct stories, each with a desk and its tier
it is ordered by TIME alone, the latest first, whatever the desk (the desks only choose which stories are on the page)
the top band holds at most six, with the militant attacks, the war, and the former minister's passing (the reader's own death before the foreign ambassador's) of the real data
the core has at least its full quotas: politics 4, sports 3, metro 2, business 2 (the data has enough of each); places the top band leaves go to politics first, as the order of importance says
no film story and no unclassified filler is on the page while the desks above have stories
with the top band short of stories, the core and then the fill take the places: the page is still eighteen
with fewer stories than places, all are shown
a desk with a quota does not take more than the quota in the first pass while others wait (politics 4 of 15 when sports has stories)
Anandabazar is read SECTION BY SECTION (state, national, metro, sports, business, world, entertainment, and the paper as a whole), each a Google News search of its own path, and listings are skipped
the Kolkata section is weighed above the West Bengal one it lies inside, so a story in both is filed as metro

the other Bengali dailies are mixed in: Sangbad Pratidin, Bartaman, Ei Samay, Aajkaal, then BBC বাংলা; each is of lower weight than any Anandabazar section, so a story both carry is Anandabazar's; no TV channel or aggregator is among them
each new paper is read as a whole through Google News' public search of its own site, and listings (a section's page, a one-word place name) are skipped
the Bengali tab is built curated: eighteen stories, each with a desk (and no chip name), 'Anandabazar Patrika' named once, and the papers that did not answer named
the other tabs are NOT curated: the English tab's stories have no desk and no tier
printed-page listings are told apart from news
